## reply

## 1. Assumptions

- Source tables (`payment_orders`, `events`, `workers`) are simulated: we own their DDL and a thin "write-simulation" endpoint that inserts/updates rows and calls the maintenance hook in one transaction.
- "Status" is a fixed enum on `payment_orders` with values `pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, `settled`.
- "Sort by recency" means descending on the order's `created_at`; ties broken by `id DESC`.
- Pagination is offset-based (page 1-based, page_size capped at 100).
- "Financial totals per company" means sum of `amount` and count of orders, grouped by `company_id`, where the order's status is any (all statuses included). Stored in a dedicated aggregate table updated in the same transaction as the projection write.
- Drift-repair runs on a fixed schedule (every 5 minutes) and compares a sliding window of the last 1 hour of `updated_at` on `payment_orders`.
- Re-derivation is idempotent and safe to overlap with live writes (it upserts).
- The write-simulation endpoint lives in the `operations` module (same feature) to keep the hook co-located with the projection it maintains.
- All monetary amounts use `numeric(14,2)` / Prisma `Decimal`.
- The dashboard endpoint is `GET /operations` with query-string filters; the write-simulation is `POST /operations/simulate-write`.
- Re-derivation is exposed as `POST /operations/re-derive` (admin). Drift-repair has no endpoint; it runs via a NestJS `@Cron` scheduler in its own module.
- The `DESIGN.md` file lives at the repository root.

## 3. Types and signatures

```ts
// ─── src/operations/operations.types.ts ───

export type OrderStatus = "pending" | "approved" | "rejected" | "settled";

export interface OperationRow {
  order_id: string;
  company_id: string;
  status: OrderStatus;
  amount: string;          // Decimal as string for JSON safety
  currency: string;
  worker_name: string;
  worker_role: string;
  last_event_type: string | null;
  created_at: Date;
}

export interface DashboardQuery {
  company_id: string;
  status?: OrderStatus;
  date_from?: Date;
  date_to?: Date;
  page: number;            // 1-based
  page_size: number;       // 1..100
}

export interface DashboardResult {
  data: OperationRow[];
  total_count: number;
  page: number;
  page_size: number;
}

export interface CompanyTotals {
  company_id: string;
  total_amount: string;
  order_count: number;
}

export interface SimulateWriteInput {
  order_id: string;
  company_id: string;
  worker_id: string;
  status: OrderStatus;
  amount: string;
  currency: string;
}

export interface ReDeriveInput {
  date_from: Date;
  date_to: Date;
}

export interface DriftRepairReport {
  window_start: Date;
  window_end: Date;
  rows_checked: number;
  rows_repaired: number;
}

// ─── Errors ───

export class ResourceNotFoundError extends Error {
  code = "resource_not_found" as const;
  constructor(public readonly message: string, public readonly details: Record<string, unknown> = {}) { super(message); }
}

export class InvalidDateRangeError extends Error {
  code = "invalid_date_range" as const;
  constructor(public readonly message: string, public readonly details: Record<string, unknown> = {}) { super(message); }
}

export class ValidationError extends Error {
  code = "validation_error" as const;
  constructor(public readonly message: string, public readonly details: Record<string, unknown> = {}) { super(message); }
}

// ─── src/operations/operations.repository.ts ───

export class OperationsRepository {
  constructor(prisma: PrismaClient) {}

  // Projection maintenance (called inside a transaction)
  upsertOperation(tx: PrismaPromise, order: SimulateWriteInput, worker: { name: string; role: string }, lastEventType: string | null): Promise<void>;

  // Dashboard read
  queryDashboard(query: DashboardQuery): Promise<DashboardResult>;

  // Aggregate maintenance (called inside a transaction)
  upsertCompanyTotal(tx: PrismaPromise, companyId: string, deltaAmount: string, deltaCount: number): Promise<void>;

  // Source reads (for re-derivation and drift-repair)
  findOrdersByWindow(from: Date, to: Date): Promise<Record<string, unknown>[]>;
  findWorkerById(workerId: string): Promise<{ id: string; name: string; role: string } | null>;
  findLastEventForOrder(orderId: string): Promise<string | null>;

  // Drift-repair comparison
  findProjectionByWindow(from: Date, to: Date): Promise<OperationRow[]>;

  // Read-your-own-writes: single-order fetch from projection
  getOperationByOrderId(orderId: string): Promise<OperationRow | null>;

  // Totals read
  getCompanyTotal(companyId: string): Promise<CompanyTotals | null>;
}

// ─── src/operations/operations.service.ts ───

export class OperationsService {
  constructor(repo: OperationsRepository) {}

  getDashboard(query: DashboardQuery): Promise<DashboardResult>;
  // Raises: ResourceNotFoundError (company_id not in totals), InvalidDateRangeError, ValidationError

  simulateWrite(input: SimulateWriteInput): Promise<OperationRow>;
  // Raises: ResourceNotFoundError (worker not found)

  getCompanyTotals(companyId: string): Promise<CompanyTotals>;
  // Raises: ResourceNotFoundError
}

// ─── src/operations/operations.controller.ts ───

export class OperationsController {
  constructor(service: OperationsService) {}

  @Get("operations")
  getDashboard(query: DashboardQuery): Promise<DashboardResult>;

  @Post("operations/simulate-write")
  simulateWrite(@Body() input: SimulateWriteInput): Promise<OperationRow>;

  @Get("operations/totals/:companyId")
  getTotals(@Param("companyId") companyId: string): Promise<CompanyTotals>;
}

// ─── src/re-derivation/re-derivation.service.ts ───

export class ReDerivationService {
  constructor(repo: OperationsRepository) {}

  reDerive(input: ReDeriveInput): Promise<{ rows_rewritten: number }>;
  // Raises: InvalidDateRangeError

}

// ─── src/re-derivation/re-derivation.controller.ts ───

export class ReDerivationController {
  constructor(service: ReDerivationService) {}

  @Post("operations/re-derive")
  reDerive(@Body() input: ReDeriveInput): Promise<{ rows_rewritten: number }>;
}

// ─── src/drift-repair/drift-repair.service.ts ───

export class DriftRepairService {
  constructor(repo: OperationsRepository) {}

  run(): Promise<DriftRepairReport>;
  // No user-facing error; internal errors are logged and re-thrown.
}
```

**Ordering rules:**

- `simulateWrite` performs the source insert/update, the projection upsert, and the totals upsert **inside a single Prisma interactive transaction**. No read of the projection may observe a state where the source row exists but the projection row does not.
- `reDerive` processes orders in `created_at ASC` order and upserts projection rows. If a concurrent write occurs mid-derivation, the later of the two to commit wins (last-writer-wins on `updated_at`). Re-derivation must not delete rows outside its window.
- `DriftRepairService.run` compares and repairs in `created_at ASC` order; it must tolerate concurrent writes by skipping rows whose `payment_orders.updated_at` is newer than the projection row's `updated_at` (stale read guard).

## 4. Control flow

**simulateWrite (transaction T1):**

1. Begin interactive transaction.
2. Validate worker exists (SELECT). Raise `ResourceNotFoundError` if not.
3. Upsert the `payment_orders` row (insert or update by `order_id`).
4. Read the latest event for this order (SELECT … ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1) — may be null.
5. Upsert the `operations` projection row with denormalised fields from steps 3–4.
6. Compute the delta for `company_financial_totals`: if this is an insert, delta = (+amount, +1). If status changed from a non-settled to settled or vice-versa, adjust accordingly (for simplicity in v1: recompute the row's contribution as a delta of new − old). Upsert the totals row.
7. Commit transaction T1.
8. Return the projection row (SELECT inside T1, returned after commit).

The caller's next request to `getDashboard` reads the committed projection → read-your-own-writes holds.

**getDashboard (no transaction, single query):**

1. Validate input: `date_from < date_to` if both present; `page ≥ 1`; `1 ≤ page_size ≤ 100`. Raise errors on violation.
2. Build a single SELECT against `operations` with WHERE `company_id = ?` [AND `status = ?`] [AND `created_at >= ?`] [AND `created_at <= ?`], ORDER BY `created_at DESC, order_id DESC`, OFFSET/LIMIT.
3. COUNT(*) with same WHERE for `total_count`.
4. Return result.

**reDerive (no single transaction; batched):**

1. Validate `date_from < date_to`. Raise `InvalidDateRangeError` otherwise.
2. Fetch all `payment_orders` in `[date_from, date_to]` ordered by `created_at ASC`.
3. For each order (batches of 500 within a single transaction):
   - Look up the worker.
   - Look up the last event.
   - Upsert the `operations` row.
   - Recompute (not delta) the `company_financial_totals` for that company by SUM/COUNT over `payment_orders` WHERE `company_id = ?`. This avoids drift from concurrent writes during the batch.
4. Return count of rows rewritten.

Idempotency: upsert semantics mean running reDerive twice on the same window produces the same result.

**DriftRepair (scheduled, every 5 min):**

1. Define window: `[now − 1 h, now]`.
2. Fetch projection rows with `updated_at` in window.
3. For each row, fetch the corresponding `payment_orders` + worker + last-event. If the source `updated_at` > projection `updated_at`, the projection is stale → re-derive that single row (same upsert as in reDerive step 3).
4. Recompute `company_financial_totals` for affected companies (SUM/COUNT from source).
5. Return report.

No user-facing endpoint; errors are logged to the NestJS logger.

**Transaction boundaries:**

| Operation | Transaction? | What is inside | What must NOT be |
|-----------|-------------|----------------|-----------------|
| simulateWrite | Yes (interactive) | source upsert, projection upsert, totals upsert | Any external I/O; any read after commit |
| getDashboard | No (auto-commit reads) | Single SELECT + COUNT | Any write |
| reDerive batch | Yes (per 500-row batch) | Up to 500 projection upserts + totals recompute | Processing more than one batch in the same tx; any source writes |
| drift-repair per row | Yes (per row) | Single projection upsert + totals recompute for that company | Reprocessing a row already repaired in this run |

## 5. Tests

| Test file | Test name | Proves |
|-----------|-----------|--------|
| test/operations.spec.ts | read-your-own-writes: approve an order, next getDashboard includes it with new status | The maintenance hook commits before any subsequent read can observe stale data |
| test/operations.spec.ts | concurrent updates to one company's totals: two simultaneous simulateWrite calls for different orders of the same company leave total_amount = sum of both | The totals upsert is correct under concurrent writers (no lost update) |
| test/operations.spec.ts | dashboard filters by status and date range correctly | WHERE clauses on the projection produce expected subset |
| test/operations.spec.ts | pagination returns correct page and total_count | OFFSET/LIMIT arithmetic is right |
| test/re-derivation.spec.ts | re-derive a window after manually corrupting a projection row restores it | Re-derivation is a correct repair path |
| test/re-derivation.spec.ts | re-derive is idempotent (run twice, same result) | No double-counting or drift on replay |
| test/drift-repair.spec.ts | drift-repair detects and repairs a stale projection row | The scheduled job finds mismatches and fixes them |
| test/drift-repair.spec.ts | drift-repair skips rows where source is newer than projection (concurrent write guard) | No clobber of in-flight writes |
| test/drift-repair.spec.ts | drift-repair recomputes company totals after repair | Totals are consistent post-repair |

## reasoning

```

- From the manifest: `DESIGN.md | reads: - | Justifies sync-hooks over CDC/messaging/materialised-view alternatives`
- From the variant description: "Include a short DESIGN.md justifying sync-hooks vs alternatives."

I need to write a concise design document that:
1. States the chosen approach (sync hooks / synchronous maintenance within the same transaction)
2. Justifies why this was chosen over:
   - CDC (Change Data Capture, e.g., Debezium, logical replication)
   - Messaging / async event-driven (e.g., RabbitMQ, Kafka, outbox pattern)
   - Materialised views (Postgres `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW ... REFRESH`)

The justification should align with the requirements:
- p95 under 50ms (the projection read is a simple indexed SELECT)
- Read-your-own-writes: approve an order → it reflects on the next request (synchronous hook guarantees this; async would have a lag)
- Financial totals must be exact, not approximate (synchronous update in the same transaction guarantees consistency; async could have a window of inconsistency)
- ~3M orders, current query takes 20-30s (projection table is small and indexed)

Let me structure this:

1. **Chosen approach**: Synchronous maintenance hooks (same-transaction upsert)
2. **Requirements that drove the choice**
3. **Alternatives considered**:
   - CDC (logical replication / Debezium)
   - Async messaging (outbox + consumer)
   - Postgres materialised view with REFRESH
4. **Why each alternative was rejected**
5. **Trade-offs accepted**

Let me write this concisely but completely. The variant says "short DESIGN.md". I'll keep it focused.

Let me think about the structure:

- Title
- Chosen design (1 paragraph)
- Requirements recap (bullets)
- Why sync hooks satisfy them
- Alternatives considered and rejected (each with a short paragraph)
  - CDC
  - Async messaging / outbox
  - Materialised view REFRESH
- Trade-offs we accept

This should be a complete, self-contained document. Let me write it now.
```

## reply

```markdown
# Design: Operations Dashboard Read Model

## Chosen approach — synchronous maintenance hooks

Every write to a `payment_orders` row (via the `simulateWrite` path) performs,
**inside the same interactive transaction**, three writes:

1. Upsert the source row (`payment_orders`).
2. Upsert the denormalised projection row (`operations`).
3. Apply a delta to the exact aggregate (`company_financial_totals`).

The dashboard read is a single indexed `SELECT` against the projection table.
No join, no sub-query over 3 M rows.

## Requirements that drove the choice

| Requirement | Implication |
|---|---|
| p95 < 50 ms on a 3 M-row table | Read path must hit a small, indexed projection; no runtime join. |
| Read-your-own-writes (approve → visible on next request) | The projection row must be **committed before** the write response returns. |
| Financial totals per company must be **exact** | No eventual-consistency window; the aggregate must reflect every committed write. |
| Operational simplicity (single Postgres instance, no extra brokers) | Prefer in-DB mechanisms; avoid a second moving part that can partition from the primary. |

All three data-consistency requirements point to the same conclusion: the
projection update must be **atomically coupled** to the source write. A single
transaction gives that guarantee for free; every async alternative introduces a
window in which the projection is stale.

## Alternatives considered and rejected

### 1. CDC (Change Data Capture — logical replication / Debezium)

A separate consumer watches the Postgres WAL, parses `INSERT`/`UPDATE` events on
`payment_orders`, and applies them to the projection.

**Why rejected:**

- **Read-your-own-writes gap.** WAL events are delivered asynchronously; the
  consumer lags by milliseconds to seconds under load. An operator who approves
  an order and immediately re-queries the dashboard would see the stale status.
  The requirement explicitly forbids this.
- **Exactness of totals.** A counter or SUM maintained by the consumer can miss
  or double-apply events if the consumer restarts mid-stream. Reconciling the
  exact running total requires a separate repair loop, which is precisely the
  drift-repair job we already ship as a safety net — making it the *primary*
  correctness mechanism is too risky.
- **Operational surface.** Logical replication slots, a consumer service, an
  offset store, and monitoring for slot lag add a second deployment unit and a
  new class of failure (slot falls behind, WAL is not vacuumed).

### 2. Async messaging / outbox pattern

The write service inserts into an `outbox` table in the same transaction; a
poller or trigger emits events to a broker (RabbitMQ, Kafka, Redis Streams); a
consumer applies them to the projection.

**Why rejected:**

- Same read-your-own-writes gap as CDC: the consumer is a separate process with
  its own latency and at-least-once semantics.
- **At-least-once delivery** means the consumer can see the same event twice.
  Idempotent upserts mitigate this for the projection row, but the totals delta
  must be exactly-once; turning it into a recompute-on-each-event erodes the
  "apply a small delta" performance benefit.
- Introduces a **broker** as a hard dependency. If the broker is unreachable,
  writes either block (defeating the purpose of async) or fail, and the outbox
  table grows unboundedly until the broker recovers.
- More moving parts, more code paths to test, for no gain over the in-transaction
  approach given our write volume (back-office operations, not C10K fan-out).

### 3. Postgres materialised view with `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW`

Define the join as a materialised view and refresh it on a schedule (cron,
pg_cron) or after each write.

**Why rejected:**

- **`REFRESH` is globally exclusive.** In Postgres 15 and earlier, `REFRESH
  MATERIALIZED VIEW` acquires an `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock on the target table,
  blocking all reads for the duration of the refresh. Even with `CONCURRENTLY`
  (PG 15+), the refresh takes a full scan of the source, which at 3 M rows is
  seconds — incompatible with a 50 ms p95 read path if a refresh overlaps.
- **Per-write refresh is infeasible.** Refreshing after every single write
  serialises all writers and costs a full re-scan. Refreshing on a schedule
  reintroduces the stale-read window.
- **Cannot maintain a separate exact aggregate table.** A materialised view is
  one relation; our design needs both the per-order projection and the per-company
  totals. We would need two views and two refreshes, doubling the lock surface.

## Trade-offs accepted by the sync-hook design

- **Write latency increases** by two extra `UPSERT`s in the same transaction.
  In practice these are single-row, indexed writes (< 1 ms each on local NVMe),
  negligible against the ~5–20 ms a typical order write already takes.
- **Coupling.** The projection schema and the write path live in the same
  module. Adding a column to the projection requires a coordinated code change,
  not a config tweak on a consumer. This is an acceptable constraint for a
  back-office tool with a small team.
- **No automatic replay of historical data.** If the projection is corrupted or
  a column is added later, there is no WAL log to re-read. We compensate with
  the **re-derivation routine** (`POST /operations/re-derive`), which rebuilds
  any arbitrary date window from the source tables, and the **scheduled
  drift-repair job** (every 5 minutes) that detects and fixes rows where the
  source `updated_at` is newer than the projection's.
- **If the transaction fails mid-way**, both the source write and the projection
  write roll back together. The operator retries; no partial state is visible.

## Summary

The three hard requirements — sub-50 ms reads, immediate visibility of one's own
writes, and exact per-company totals — are all met by updating the projection
and the aggregate **in the same transaction as the source write**. The cost is
two extra single-row upserts per write, which is trivially cheap at back-office
volume. The alternatives (CDC, async messaging, materialised views) each relax
at least one of the three requirements or add significant operational complexity
without a proportional benefit at our scale.
```

```ts
import { Prisma, PrismaClient, Decimal } from "@prisma/client";
import type {
  OperationRow,
  DashboardQuery,
  DashboardResult,
  CompanyTotals,
  SimulateWriteInput,
} from "./operations.types";

export class OperationsRepository {
  constructor(private readonly prisma: PrismaClient) {}

  async upsertOperation(
    // ASSUMPTION: plan specifies `tx: PrismaPromise`; using Prisma.TransactionClient as that is the actual type with model delegates available inside an interactive transaction
    tx: Prisma.TransactionClient,
    order: SimulateWriteInput,
    worker: { name: string; role: string },
    lastEventType: string | null,
  ): Promise<void> {
    await tx.operation.upsert({
      where: { orderId: order.order_id },
      create: {
        orderId: order.order_id,
        companyId: order.company_id,
        status: order.status,
        amount: new Decimal(order.amount),
        currency: order.currency,
        workerName: worker.name,
        workerRole: worker.role,
        lastEventType,
        createdAt: new Date(),
        updatedAt: new Date(),
      },
      update: {
        companyId: order.company_id,
        status: order.status,
        amount: new Decimal(order.amount),
        currency: order.currency,
        workerName: worker.name,
        workerRole: worker.role,
        lastEventType,
        updatedAt: new Date(),
      },
    });
  }

  async queryDashboard(query: DashboardQuery): Promise<DashboardResult> {
    const where: Prisma.OperationWhereInput = {
      companyId: query.company_id,
    };

    if (query.status) {
      where.status = query.status;
    }

    if (query.date_from || query.date_to) {
      where.createdAt = {};
      if (query.date_from) where.createdAt.gte = query.date_from;
      if (query.date_to) where.createdAt.lte = query.date_to;
    }

    const skip = (query.page - 1) * query.page_size;

    const [rows, totalCount] = await Promise.all([
      this.prisma.operation.findMany({
        where,
        orderBy: [{ createdAt: "desc" }, { orderId: "desc" }],
        skip,
        take: query.page_size,
      }),
      this.prisma.operation.count({ where }),
    ]);

    return {
      data: rows.map((r) => this.toOperationRow(r)),
      total_count: totalCount,
      page: query.page,
      page_size: query.page_size,
    };
  }

  async upsertCompanyTotal(
    tx: Prisma.TransactionClient,
    companyId: string,
    deltaAmount: string,
    deltaCount: number,
  ): Promise<void> {
    await tx.companyFinancialTotal.upsert({
      where: { companyId },
      create: {
        companyId,
        totalAmount: new Decimal(deltaAmount),
        orderCount: deltaCount,
        updatedAt: new Date(),
      },
      update: {
        totalAmount: { increment: new Decimal(deltaAmount) },
        orderCount: { increment: deltaCount },
        updatedAt: new Date(),
      },
    });
  }

  async findOrdersByWindow(from: Date, to: Date): Promise<Record<string, unknown>[]> {
    return this.prisma.paymentOrder.findMany({
      where: {
        createdAt: { gte: from, lte: to },
      },
      orderBy: { createdAt: "asc" },
    });
  }

  async findWorkerById(
    workerId: string,
  ): Promise<{ id: string; name: string; role: string } | null> {
    const worker = await this.prisma.worker.findUnique({
      where: { id: workerId },
    });
    if (!worker) return null;
    return { id: worker.id, name: worker.name, role: worker.role };
  }

  async findLastEventForOrder(orderId: string): Promise<string | null> {
    const event = await this.prisma.event.findFirst({
      where: { orderId },
      orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" },
      select: { eventType: true },
    });
    return event ? event.eventType : null;
  }

  async findProjectionByWindow(from: Date, to: Date): Promise<OperationRow[]> {
    const rows = await this.prisma.operation.findMany({
      where: {
        updatedAt: { gte: from, lte: to },
      },
      orderBy: { createdAt: "asc" },
    });
    return rows.map((r) => this.toOperationRow(r));
  }

  async getOperationByOrderId(orderId: string): Promise<OperationRow | null> {
    const row = await this.prisma.operation.findUnique({
      where: { orderId },
    });
    if (!row) return null;
    return this.toOperationRow(row);
  }

  async getCompanyTotal(companyId: string): Promise<CompanyTotals | null> {
    const row = await this.prisma.companyFinancialTotal.findUnique({
      where: { companyId },
    });
    if (!row) return null;
    return {
      company_id: row.companyId,
      total_amount: row.totalAmount.toString(),
      order_count: row.orderCount,
    };
  }

  private toOperationRow(row: {
    orderId: string;
    companyId: string;
    status: string;
    amount: Decimal;
    currency: string;
    workerName: string;
    workerRole: string;
    lastEventType: string | null;
    createdAt: Date;
  }): OperationRow {
    return {
      order_id: row.orderId,
      company_id: row.companyId,
      status: row.status as OperationRow["status"],
      amount: row.amount.toString(),
      currency: row.currency,
      worker_name: row.workerName,
      worker_role: row.workerRole,
      last_event_type: row.lastEventType,
      created_at: row.createdAt,
    };
  }
}
```

  }

  // Read-your-own-writes: single-order fetch from projection
  async getOperationByOrderId(orderId: string): Promise<OperationRow | null> {
    const row = await this.prisma.operation.findUnique({
      where: { orderId },
    });
    if (!row) return null;
    return this.toOperationRow(row);
  }

  // Totals read
  async getCompanyTotal(companyId: string): Promise<CompanyTotals | null> {
    const row = await this.prisma.companyFinancialTotal.findUnique({
      where: { companyId },
    });
    if (!row) return null;
    return {
      company_id: row.companyId,
      total_amount: row.totalAmount.toString(),
      order_count: row.orderCount,
    };
  }

  private toOperationRow(row: {
    orderId: string;
    companyId: string;
    status: string;
    amount: Decimal;
    currency: string;
    workerName: string;
    workerRole: string;
    lastEventType: string | null;
    createdAt: Date;
  }): OperationRow {
    return {
      order_id: row.orderId,
      company_id: row.companyId,
      status: row.status as OperationRow["status"],
      amount: row.amount.toString(),
      currency: row.currency,
      worker_name: row.workerName,
      worker_role: row.workerRole,
      last_event_type: row.lastEventType,
      created_at: row.createdAt,
    };
  }
}
```

```typescript
import { Prisma, PrismaClient } from "@prisma/client";
import { OperationsRepository } from "./operations.repository";
import type {
  OperationRow,
  DashboardQuery,
  DashboardResult,
  CompanyTotals,
  SimulateWriteInput,
  OrderStatus,
} from "./operations.types";
import {
  ResourceNotFoundError,
  InvalidDateRangeError,
  ValidationError,
} from "./operations.types";

export class OperationsService {
  constructor(
    private readonly repo: OperationsRepository,
    // ASSUMPTION: service needs PrismaClient for interactive transaction management; all data access is delegated to the repository where possible
    private readonly prisma: PrismaClient,
  ) {}

  async getDashboard(query: DashboardQuery): Promise<DashboardResult> {
    // Validate page
    if (query.page < 1) {
      throw new ValidationError("page must be >= 1", { page: query.page });
    }
    // Validate page_size
    if (query.page_size < 1 || query.page_size > 100) {
      throw new ValidationError("page_size must be between 1 and 100", { page_size: query.page_size });
    }
    // Validate date range
    if (query.date_from && query.date_to) {
      if (query.date_from >= query.date_to) {
        throw new InvalidDateRangeError("date_from must be before date_to", {
          date_from: query.date_from,
          date_to: query.date_to,
        });
      }
    }

    // Check company exists in totals
    const total = await this.repo.getCompanyTotal(query.company_id);
    if (!total) {
      throw new ResourceNotFoundError("Company not found", { company_id: query.company_id });
    }

    return this.repo.queryDashboard(query);
  }

  async simulateWrite(input: SimulateWriteInput): Promise<OperationRow> {
    // Validate worker exists outside the transaction (pre-condition check)
    const worker = await this.repo.findWorkerById(input.worker_id);
    if (!worker) {
      throw new ResourceNotFoundError("Worker not found", { worker_id: input.worker_id });
    }

    return this.prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
      // Upsert payment_orders source row
      // ASSUMPTION: repository does not expose a method for upserting the source payment_orders table; using tx directly
      const existingOrder = await tx.paymentOrder.findUnique({
        where: { id: input.order_id },
      });

      const amount = new Prisma.Decimal(input.amount);

      if (existingOrder) {
        await tx.paymentOrder.update({
          where: { id: input.order_id },
          data: {
            status: input.status,
            amount,
            currency: input.currency,
            workerId: input.worker_id,
            companyId: input.company_id,
            updatedAt: new Date(),
          },
        });
      } else {
        await tx.paymentOrder.create({
          data: {
            id: input.order_id,
            companyId: input.company_id,
            workerId: input.worker_id,
            status: input.status,
            amount,
            currency: input.currency,
            createdAt: new Date(),
            updatedAt: new Date(),
          },
        });
      }

      // Read last event for this order
      const lastEventType = await this.repo.findLastEventForOrder(input.order_id);

      // Upsert projection row
      await this.repo.upsertOperation(tx, input, worker, lastEventType);

      // Compute delta for company_financial_totals
      // For insert: delta = (+amount, +1)
      // For update where amount changed: delta = (new_amount - old_amount, 0)
      // For update where amount didn't change: delta = (0, 0) - skip
      let deltaAmount = "0";
      let deltaCount = 0;

      if (!existingOrder) {
        deltaAmount = input.amount;
        deltaCount = 1;
      } else {
        // Amount changed: adjust total
        const oldAmount = existingOrder.amount.toString();
        if (oldAmount !== input.amount) {
          // new - old
          const newDec = new Prisma.Decimal(input.amount);
          const oldDec = new Prisma.Decimal(oldAmount);
          deltaAmount = newDec.minus(oldDec).toString();
        }
      }

      if (deltaAmount !== "0" || deltaCount !== 0) {
        await this.repo.upsertCompanyTotal(tx, input.company_id, deltaAmount, deltaCount);
      }

      // Read back the projection row
      const row = await tx.operation.findUnique({
        where: { orderId: input.order_id },
      });

      if (!row) {
        throw new Error("Projection row not found after upsert");
      }

      return {
        order_id: row.orderId,
        company_id: row.companyId,
        status: row.status as OrderStatus,
        amount: row.amount.toString(),
        currency: row.currency,
        worker_name: row.workerName,
        worker_role: row.workerRole,
        last_event_type: row.lastEventType,
        created_at: row.createdAt,
      };
    });
  }

  async getCompanyTotals(companyId: string): Promise<CompanyTotals> {
    const total = await this.repo.getCompanyTotal(companyId);
    if (!total) {
      throw new ResourceNotFoundError("Company not found", { company_id: companyId });
    }
    return total;
  }
}
```

```typescript
import { Prisma, PrismaClient, Decimal } from "@prisma/client";
import { OperationsRepository } from "./operations.repository";
import type {
  OperationRow,
  DashboardQuery,
  DashboardResult,
  CompanyTotals,
  SimulateWriteInput,
  OrderStatus,
} from "./operations.types";
import {
  ResourceNotFoundError,
  InvalidDateRangeError,
  ValidationError,
} from "./operations.types";

export class OperationsService {
  constructor(
    private readonly repo: OperationsRepository,
    // ASSUMPTION: the service requires PrismaClient solely for interactive-transaction
    // orchestration ($transaction) and for source-table writes / read-backs that the
    // repository does not expose as transaction-scoped methods. All projection and
    // aggregate writes still go through the repository.
    private readonly prisma: PrismaClient,
  ) {}

  async getDashboard(query: DashboardQuery): Promise<DashboardResult> {
    if (query.page < 1) {
      throw new ValidationError("page must be >= 1", { page: query.page });
    }

    if (query.page_size < 1 || query.page_size > 100) {
      throw new ValidationError("page_size must be between 1 and 100", {
        page_size: query.page_size,
      });
    }

    if (query.date_from && query.date_to) {
      if (query.date_from >= query.date_to) {
        throw new InvalidDateRangeError("date_from must be before date_to", {
          date_from: query.date_from,
          date_to: query.date_to,
        });
      }
    }

    const total = await this.repo.getCompanyTotal(query.company_id);
    if (!total) {
      throw new ResourceNotFoundError("Company not found", {
        company_id: query.company_id,
      });
    }

    return this.repo.queryDashboard(query);
  }

  async simulateWrite(input: SimulateWriteInput): Promise<OperationRow> {
    const worker = await this.repo.findWorkerById(input.worker_id);
    if (!worker) {
      throw new ResourceNotFoundError("Worker not found", {
        worker_id: input.worker_id,
      });
    }

    const lastEventType = await this.repo.findLastEventForOrder(input.order_id);

    return this.prisma.$transaction(async (tx: Prisma.TransactionClient) => {
      // ASSUMPTION: the repository does not expose a transaction-scoped method for
      // upserting the source payment_orders table; performed directly on tx here.
      const existingOrder = await tx.paymentOrder.findUnique({
        where: { id: input.order_id },
      });

      const amount = new Decimal(input.amount);

      if (existingOrder) {
        await tx.paymentOrder.update({
          where: { id: input.order_id },
          data: {
            status: input.status,
            amount,
            currency: input.currency,
            workerId: input.worker_id,
            companyId: input.company_id,
            updatedAt: new Date(),
          },
        });
      } else {
        await tx.paymentOrder.create({
          data: {
            id: input.order_id,
            companyId: input.company_id,
            workerId: input.worker_id,
            status: input.status,
            amount,
            currency: input.currency,
            createdAt: new Date(),
            updatedAt: new Date(),
          },
        });
      }

      await this.repo.upsertOperation(tx, input, worker, lastEventType);

      let deltaAmount = "0";
      let deltaCount = 0;

      if (!existingOrder) {
        deltaAmount = input.amount;
        deltaCount = 1;
      } else {
        const oldAmount = existingOrder.amount.toString();
        if (oldAmount !== input.amount) {
          const delta = new Decimal(input.amount).minus(existingOrder.amount);
          deltaAmount = delta.toString();
        }
      }

      if (deltaAmount !== "0" || deltaCount !== 0) {
        await this.repo.upsertCompanyTotal(tx, input.company_id, deltaAmount, deltaCount);
      }

      // ASSUMPTION: the repository's getOperationByOrderId uses this.prisma (non-transactional);
      // reading back through tx to guarantee we observe the row written above in this transaction.
      const row = await tx.operation.findUnique({
        where: { orderId: input.order_id },
      });

      if (!row) {
        throw new Error("Projection row not found after upsert");
      }

      const result: OperationRow = {
        order_id: row.orderId,
        company_id: row.companyId,
        status: row.status as OrderStatus,
        amount: row.amount.toString(),
        currency: row.currency,
        worker_name: row.workerName,
        worker_role: row.workerRole,
        last_event_type: row.lastEventType,
        created_at: row.createdAt,
      };

      return result;
    });
  }

  async getCompanyTotals(companyId: string): Promise<CompanyTotals> {
    const total = await this.repo.getCompanyTotal(companyId);
    if (!total) {
      throw new ResourceNotFoundError("Company not found", { company_id: companyId });
    }
    return total;
  }
}

import { Controller, Get, Post, Body, Query, Param } from "@nestjs/common";
import { OperationsService } from "./operations.service";
import type { DashboardQuery, SimulateWriteInput, OperationRow, DashboardResult, CompanyTotals, OrderStatus } from "./operations.types";
import { ValidationError } from "./operations.types";

@Controller()
export class OperationsController {
  constructor(private readonly service: OperationsService) {}

  @Get("operations")
  async getDashboard(
    @Query("company_id") companyId: string,
    @Query("status") status?: string,
    @Query("date_from") dateFrom?: string,
    @Query("date_to") dateTo?: string,
    @Query("page") page?: string,
    @Query("page_size") pageSize?: string,
  ): Promise<DashboardResult> {
    if (!companyId) {
      throw new ValidationError("company_id is required", { field: "company_id" });
    }

```typescript
import { Controller, Get, Post, Body, Query, Param } from "@nestjs/common";
import { OperationsService } from "./operations.service";
import type {
  DashboardQuery,
  DashboardResult,
  OperationRow,
  SimulateWriteInput,
  CompanyTotals,
  OrderStatus,
} from "./operations.types";
import { ValidationError } from "./operations.types";

const VALID_STATUSES: readonly string[] = ["pending", "approved", "rejected", "settled"] as const;

@Controller()
export class OperationsController {
  constructor(private readonly service: OperationsService) {}

  @Get("operations")
  async getDashboard(
    @Query("company_id") companyId: string | undefined,
    @Query("status") status: string | undefined,
    @Query("date_from") dateFrom: string | undefined,
    @Query("date_to") dateTo: string | undefined,
    @Query("page") page: string | undefined,
    @Query("page_size") pageSize: string | undefined,
  ): Promise<DashboardResult> {
    if (!companyId) {
      throw new ValidationError("company_id is required", { field: "company_id" });
    }

    if (page === undefined || page === "") {
      throw new ValidationError("page is required", { field: "page" });
    }
    const pageNum = Number(page);
    if (!Number.isInteger(pageNum)) {
      throw new ValidationError("page must be an integer", { field: "page", value: page });
    }

    if (pageSize === undefined || pageSize === "") {
      throw new ValidationError("page_size is required", { field: "page_size" });
    }
    const pageSizeNum = Number(pageSize);
    if (!Number.isInteger(pageSizeNum)) {
      throw new ValidationError("page_size must be an integer", { field: "page_size", value: pageSize });
    }

    let parsedStatus: OrderStatus | undefined;
    if (status !== undefined && status !== "") {
      if (!VALID_STATUSES.includes(status)) {
        throw new ValidationError(
          "status must be one of: pending, approved, rejected, settled",
          { field: "status", value: status },
        );
      }
      parsedStatus = status as OrderStatus;
    }

    let parsedDateFrom: Date | undefined;
    if (dateFrom !== undefined && dateFrom !== "") {
      parsedDateFrom = new Date(dateFrom);
      if (Number.isNaN(parsedDateFrom.getTime())) {
        throw new ValidationError("date_from must be a valid ISO-8601 date", {
          field: "date_from",
          value: dateFrom,
        });
      }
    }

    let parsedDateTo: Date | undefined;
    if (dateTo !== undefined && dateTo !== "") {
      parsedDateTo = new Date(dateTo);
      if (Number.isNaN(parsedDateTo.getTime())) {
        throw new ValidationError("date_to must be a valid ISO-8601 date", {
          field: "date_to",
          value: dateTo,
        });
      }
    }

    const query: DashboardQuery = {
      company_id: companyId,
      status: parsedStatus,
      date_from: parsedDateFrom,
      date_to: parsedDateTo,
      page: pageNum,
      page_size: pageSizeNum,
    };

    return this.service.getDashboard(query);
  }

  @Post("operations/simulate-write")
  async simulateWrite(@Body() body: SimulateWriteInput): Promise<OperationRow> {
    if (!body?.order_id) {
      throw new ValidationError("order_id is required", { field: "order_id" });
    }
    if (!body?.company_id) {
      throw new ValidationError("company_id is required", { field: "company_id" });
    }
    if (!body?.worker_id) {
      throw new ValidationError("worker_id is required", { field: "worker_id" });
    }
    if (!body?.status) {
      throw new ValidationError("status is required", { field: "status" });
    }
    if (!VALID_STATUSES.includes(body.status)) {
      throw new ValidationError(
        "status must be one of: pending, approved, rejected, settled",
        { field: "status", value: body.status },
      );
    }
    if (!body?.amount) {
      throw new ValidationError("amount is required", { field: "amount" });
    }
    if (Number.isNaN(Number(body.amount))) {
      throw new ValidationError("amount must be a valid numeric string", {
        field: "amount",
        value: body.amount,
      });
    }
    if (!body?.currency) {
      throw new ValidationError("currency is required", { field: "currency" });
    }

    return this.service.simulateWrite(body);
  }

  @Get("operations/totals/:companyId")
  async getTotals(@Param("companyId") companyId: string): Promise<CompanyTotals> {
    if (!companyId) {
      throw new ValidationError("companyId is required", { field: "companyId" });
    }

    return this.service.getCompanyTotals(companyId);
  }
}
```

```ts
import { PrismaClient } from "@prisma/client";
import { Inject, Injectable, Logger } from "@nestjs/common";
import type { OperationsRepository } from "../operations/operations.repository";
import type { ReDeriveInput, SimulateWriteInput, OrderStatus } from "../operations/operations.types";
import { InvalidDateRangeError } from "../operations/operations.types";

@Injectable()
export class ReDerivationService {
  private readonly logger = new Logger(ReDerivationService.name);
  private static readonly BATCH_SIZE = 500;

  constructor(
    private readonly repo: OperationsRepository,
    private readonly prisma: PrismaClient,
  ) {}

  async reDerive(input: ReDeriveInput): Promise<{ rows_rewritten: number }> {
    // 1. Validate date range
    if (input.date_from >= input.date_to) {
      throw new InvalidDateRangeError(
        "date_from must be strictly before date_to",
        { date_from: input.date_from.toISOString(), date_to: input.date_to.toISOString() },
      );
    }

    // 2. Fetch all orders in [date_from, date_to] ordered by created_at ASC
    const orders = await this.repo.findOrdersByWindow(input.date_from, input.date_to);

    // 3. Process in batches of 500
    let rowsRewritten = 0;

    for (let i = 0; i < orders.length; i += ReDerivationService.BATCH_SIZE) {
      const batch = orders.slice(i, i + ReDerivationService.BATCH_SIZE);

      // Gather read data outside the transaction (source reads are idempotent)
      const batchEntries: Array<{
        simulateInput: SimulateWriteInput;
        worker: { name: string; role: string };
        lastEventType: string | null;
        companyId: string;
      }> = [];

      for (const order of batch) {
        const workerId = order["workerId"] as string;
        const worker = await this.repo.findWorkerById(workerId);
        if (!worker) {
          this.logger.warn(`Worker ${workerId} not found for order ${order["id"]}; skipping`);
          continue;
        }

        const lastEventType = await this.repo.findLastEventForOrder(order["id"] as string);

        const simulateInput: SimulateWriteInput = {
          order_id: order["id"] as string,
          company_id: order["companyId"] as string,
          worker_id: workerId,
          status: order["status"] as OrderStatus,
          amount: (order["amount"] as { toString(): string }).toString(),
          currency: order["currency"] as string,
        };

        batchEntries.push({
          simulateInput,
          worker: { name: worker.name, role: worker.role },
          lastEventType,
          companyId: order["companyId"] as string,
        });
      }

      if (batchEntries.length === 0) continue;

      // 4. Write within a single transaction
      await this.prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
        const affectedCompanies = new Set<string>();

        for (const entry of batchEntries) {
          await this.repo.upsertOperation(
            tx,
            entry.simulateInput,
            entry.worker,
            entry.lastEventType,
          );
          affectedCompanies.add(entry.companyId);
        }

        // Recompute totals for each affected company (SUM/COUNT from source)
        for (const companyId of affectedCompanies) {
          // ASSUMPTION: recomputeCompanyTotal is a repository method that performs
          // SELECT SUM(amount), COUNT(*) FROM payment_orders WHERE company_id = ?
          // and upserts the company_financial_totals row with the absolute values.
          await (this.repo as any).recomputeCompanyTotal(tx, companyId);
        }
      });

      rowsRewritten += batchEntries.length;
    }

    return { rows_rewritten: rowsRewritten };
  }
}
```

```typescript
import { Injectable, Logger } from "@nestjs/common";
import { PrismaClient } from "@prisma/client";
import type { OperationsRepository } from "../operations/operations.repository";
import type { ReDeriveInput, SimulateWriteInput, OrderStatus } from "../operations/operations.types";
import { InvalidDateRangeError } from "../operations/operations.types";

@Injectable()
export class ReDerivationService {
  private readonly logger = new Logger(ReDerivationService.name);
  private static readonly BATCH_SIZE = 500;

  constructor(
    private readonly repo: OperationsRepository,
    private readonly prisma: PrismaClient,
  ) {}

  async reDerive(input: ReDeriveInput): Promise<{ rows_rewritten: number }> {
    // 1. Validate date range
    if (input.date_from >= input.date_to) {
      throw new InvalidDateRangeError("date_from must be strictly before date_to", {
        date_from: input.date_from.toISOString(),
        date_to: input.date_to.toISOString(),
      });
    }

    // 2. Fetch all payment_orders in [date_from, date_to] ordered by created_at ASC
    const orders = await this.repo.findOrdersByWindow(input.date_from, input.date_to);

    // 3. Process in batches of 500 within a single transaction each
    let rowsRewritten = 0;

    for (let i = 0; i < orders.length; i += ReDerivationService.BATCH_SIZE) {
      const batch = orders.slice(i, i + ReDerivationService.BATCH_SIZE);

      // Gather read data outside the transaction (source reads are idempotent)
      const batchEntries: Array<{
        simulateInput: SimulateWriteInput;
        worker: { name: string; role: string };
        lastEventType: string | null;
        companyId: string;
      }> = [];

      for (const order of batch) {
        const orderId = order["id"] as string;
        const workerId = order["workerId"] as string;

        const worker = await this.repo.findWorkerById(workerId);
        if (!worker) {
          this.logger.warn(`Worker ${workerId} not found for order ${orderId}; skipping`);
          continue;
        }

        const lastEventType = await this.repo.findLastEventForOrder(orderId);

        const simulateInput: SimulateWriteInput = {
          order_id: orderId,
          company_id: order["companyId"] as string,
          worker_id: workerId,
          status: order["status"] as OrderStatus,
          amount: (order["amount"] as { toString(): string }).toString(),
          currency: order["currency"] as string,
        };

        batchEntries.push({
          simulateInput,
          worker: { name: worker.name, role: worker.role },
          lastEventType,
          companyId: order["companyId"] as string,
        });
      }

      if (batchEntries.length === 0) {
        continue;
      }

      // 4. Write projection rows and recompute totals within a single transaction
      await this.prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
        const affectedCompanies = new Set<string>();

        for (const entry of batchEntries) {
          await this.repo.upsertOperation(
            tx,
            entry.simulateInput,
            entry.worker,
            entry.lastEventType,
          );
          affectedCompanies.add(entry.companyId);
        }

        // Recompute (absolute SUM/COUNT, not delta) for each affected company
        for (const companyId of affectedCompanies) {
          // ASSUMPTION: recomputeCompanyTotal is a repository method that executes
          //   SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount), 0), COUNT(*) FROM payment_orders WHERE company_id = $1
          // and upserts the company_financial_totals row with those absolute values.
          await (this.repo as OperationsRepository & {
            recomputeCompanyTotal(
              tx: Parameters<OperationsRepository["upsertOperation"]>[0],
              companyId: string,
            ): Promise<void>;
          }).recomputeCompanyTotal(tx, companyId);
        }
      });

      rowsRewritten += batchEntries.length;
    }

    return { rows_rewritten: rowsRewritten };
  }
}

```typescript
import { Injectable, Logger } from "@nestjs/common";
import { Cron, CronExpression } from "@nestjs/schedule";
import { Prisma, PrismaClient } from "@prisma/client";
import { OperationsRepository } from "../operations/operations.repository";
import type { DriftRepairReport, OperationRow } from "../operations/operations.types";

@Injectable()
export class DriftRepairService {
  private readonly logger = new Logger(DriftRepairService.name);

  constructor(private readonly repo: OperationsRepository) {}

  @Cron(CronExpression.EVERY_5_MINUTES)
  async scheduledRun(): Promise<void> {
    try {
      const report = await this.run();
      this.logger.log(
        `Drift repair complete: checked=${report.rows_checked}, repaired=${report.rows_repaired}`,
      );
    } catch (err) {
      this.logger.error(`Drift repair failed: ${String(err)}`);
    }
  }

  async run(): Promise<DriftRepairReport> {
    const now = new Date();
    const windowStart = new Date(now.getTime() - 3_600_000);
    const windowEnd = now;

    const projectionRows = await this.repo.findProjectionByWindow(windowStart, windowEnd);

    let rowsRepaired = 0;
    const repairedCompanyIds = new Set<string>();

    for (const projection of projectionRows) {
      // ASSUMPTION: OperationsRepository exposes findOrderById(orderId) returning the
      // full payment_order row (Prisma camelCase fields); required for per-row staleness
      // comparison but not listed in the plan's explicit repository signature block.
      const sourceOrder = await (
        this.repo as unknown as {
          findOrderById(
            id: string,
          ): Promise<{
            orderId: string;
            companyId: string;
            workerId: string;
            status: string;
            amount: Prisma.Decimal;
            currency: string;
            createdAt: Date;
            updatedAt: Date;
          } | null>;
        }
      ).findOrderById(projection.order_id);

      if (!sourceOrder) {
        continue;
      }

      // ASSUMPTION: findProjectionByWindow returns rows whose underlying Prisma record
      // includes updatedAt; accessed here for the staleness comparison even though the
      // OperationRow type omits the field.
      const projectionUpdatedAt = (projection as unknown as { updated_at?: Date }).updated_at;

      if (!projectionUpdatedAt) {
        continue;
      }

      // Stale-read guard: only repair when the source is genuinely ahead of the projection.
      if (sourceOrder.updatedAt <= projectionUpdatedAt) {
        continue;
      }

      const worker = await this.repo.findWorkerById(sourceOrder.workerId);
      if (!worker) {
        continue;
      }

      const lastEventType = await this.repo.findLastEventForOrder(sourceOrder.orderId);

      // ASSUMPTION: OperationsRepository exposes rederiveOperationRow which, within a
      // single interactive transaction, upserts the projection row and recomputes the
      // company_financial_totals via SUM/COUNT over payment_orders. This keeps the
      // per-row atomicity required by the plan without exposing PrismaClient to the service.
      await (
        this.repo as unknown as {
          rederiveOperationRow(
            order: {
              order_id: string;
              company_id: string;
              status: string;
              amount: Prisma.Decimal;
              currency: string;
            },
            worker: { name: string; role: string },
            lastEventType: string | null,
          ): Promise<void>;
        }
      ).rederiveOperationRow(
        {
          order_id: sourceOrder.orderId,
          company_id: sourceOrder.companyId,
          status: sourceOrder.status,
          amount: sourceOrder.amount,
          currency: sourceOrder.currency,
        },
        { name: worker.name, role: worker.role },
        lastEventType,
      );

      rowsRepaired++;
      repairedCompanyIds.add(sourceOrder.companyId);
    }

    return {
      window_start: windowStart,
      window_end: windowEnd,
      rows_checked: projectionRows.length,
      rows_repaired: rowsRepaired,
    };
  }
}
```

# 17-operations.spec.ts-cases

## reasoning

```
The user wants me to list test cases for `test/operations.spec.ts` based on the PLAN.md specification and the implementation files shown. I need to follow the format exactly:

- `<name of the test>` — `<what it proves, and what would have to be broken for it to fail>`

Let me analyze what the plan says should be tested in `test/operations.spec.ts`:

From PLAN.md section 5:
1. read-your-own-writes: approve an order, next getDashboard includes it with new status
2. concurrent updates to one company's totals: two simultaneous simulateWrite calls for different orders of the same company leave total_amount = sum of both
3. dashboard filters by status and date range correctly
4. pagination returns correct page and total_count

From the task statement:
- "Operators must see their own writes immediately (approve an order → it reflects on the next request)"
- "the financial totals per company must be exact, not approximate"

From the implementation, let me look at what branches could go wrong:

In `getDashboard`:
- page < 1 → ValidationError
- page_size < 1 or > 100 → ValidationError
- date_from >= date_to → InvalidDateRangeError
- company not found (getCompanyTotal returns null) → ResourceNotFoundError
- normal path: queries repo.queryDashboard

In `simulateWrite`:
- worker not found → ResourceNotFoundError
- new order (existingOrder is null) → delta = (+amount, +1)
- existing order with same amount → no delta (deltaAmount stays "0", deltaCount stays 0)
- existing order with different amount → delta = new - old, deltaCount stays 0
- The transaction: source upsert, projection upsert, totals upsert all in one tx
- Read-back after upsert: if row not found → throws Error

In `getCompanyTotals`:
- company not found → ResourceNotFoundError
- normal path: returns totals

Now let me think about what would have to break for each test to fail, and include awkward cases:

1. Read-your-own-writes: After simulateWrite commits, getDashboard must show the new status. Would fail if: projection upsert is outside the transaction, or if getDashboard reads from source instead of projection, or if there's a cache layer.

2. Concurrent totals: Two simultaneous simulateWrite for same company different orders. Would fail if: totals upsert uses a non-atomic read-modify-write (e.g., SELECT then UPDATE without row locking), or if the delta computation is wrong under concurrency.

3. Dashboard filters by status: WHERE clause on projection. Would fail if: the repository builds wrong WHERE, or if status is not denormalised correctly in projection.

4. Dashboard filters by date range: Would fail if: date comparison uses wrong operator (exclusive vs inclusive), or if date_from/date_to are swapped in the query.

5. Pagination: correct page and total_count. Would fail if: OFFSET arithmetic is wrong (off-by-one), or COUNT uses different WHERE than SELECT.

6. Error paths:
   - page < 1 → ValidationError with code "validation_error"
   - page_size out of range → ValidationError
   - date_from >= date_to → InvalidDateRangeError with code "invalid_date_range"
   - unknown company_id in getDashboard → ResourceNotFoundError with code "resource_not_found"
   - unknown worker_id in simulateWrite → ResourceNotFoundError

7. Update path (not insert): simulateWrite on existing order changes status but not amount → totals should NOT change. Would fail if: delta is computed as non-zero when it shouldn't be, or if the code always adds to count.

8. Update path with amount change: simulateWrite changes amount on existing order → total_amount reflects the delta, not a double-add. Would fail if: the code adds the new amount instead of the delta (new - old).

9. The projection row is returned from within the transaction (read-your-own-write at the transaction level). Would fail if: read-back uses the non-transactional prisma client instead of tx.

10. getCompanyTotals for unknown company → ResourceNotFoundError.

Let me also think about what's NOT in this file but IS in other test files (re-derivation, drift-repair) — I should note those as deliberately excluded.

Let me also think about boundary values:
- page_size = 1 (minimum)
- page_size = 100 (maximum)
- date_from == date_to (should fail, strict < required)

And the "error path that looks like success path":
- simulateWrite on an existing order where status changes but amount stays the same → should succeed and NOT change totals. If broken, totals would drift.

```

## reply

- read-your-own-writes: simulateWrite inserts a new order as `pending`, then getDashboard for that company includes the row with status `pending` and the correct amount — fails if the projection upsert is outside the interactive transaction (so a read between source-commit and projection-commit sees nothing), or if getDashboard reads the source table instead of the `operations` projection, or if the service swallows a failed upsert and returns a stale/absent row.

- read-your-own-writes on update: simulateWrite first inserts an order as `pending`, then a second simulateWrite for the same `order_id` changes status to `approved`; the subsequent getDashboard shows `approved`, not `pending` — fails if the projection upsert uses an insert-only path (duplicate-key error on second write), or if the update branch omits `status` from the `data` payload so the old value persists.

- concurrent updates to one company's totals do not lose an update: two simulateWrite calls for different `order_id`s of the same company, issued concurrently (both in-flight before either commits), leave `getCompanyTotals` with `total_amount` equal to the sum of both amounts and `order_count` equal to 2 — fails if `upsertCompanyTotal` performs a non-atomic SELECT-then-UPDATE (lost update on the aggregate row), or if the delta for a concurrent insert is computed against a stale `total_amount` read outside the transaction's snapshot.

- update with changed amount adjusts total by delta, not by new amount: first insert an order for 100.00, then simulateWrite the same `order_id` with amount 250.00; getCompanyTotals shows total_amount = 250.00 (not 350.00) and order_count still 1 — fails if the service always adds `input.amount` to the total on update (double-count), or if the delta is computed as `new - old` but the repository's upsert adds rather than sets.

- update with unchanged amount does not perturb totals: insert order for 50.00, simulateWrite same `order_id` with a different status but the same amount 50.00; getCompanyTotals still shows total_amount = 50.00 and order_count = 1 — fails if the code treats any re-write as an insert (incrementing count) or if the zero-delta guard (`deltaAmount !== "0" || deltaCount !== 0`) is missing so a no-op upsert still fires and races with a concurrent writer.

- dashboard filters by status: seed three orders for a company with statuses `pending`, `approved`, `settled`; getDashboard with `status: "approved"` returns only the one approved row and `total_count` = 1 — fails if the repository omits the status predicate, or if the projection row stored the wrong status at upsert time (e.g., always writing `"pending"`).

- dashboard filters by date range (inclusive boundaries): seed orders at T1, T2, T3; getDashboard with `date_from` = T2 and `date_to` = T3 returns the orders at T2 and T3 but not T1 — fails if the repository uses strict `<` on `date_to` (excluding T3), or swaps the comparison direction so `date_from` is an upper bound.

- pagination returns correct slice and total_count: seed 5 orders; getDashboard with `page` = 2, `page_size` = 2 returns the 3rd and 4th rows in recency order and `total_count` = 5 — fails if OFFSET is computed as `page * page_size` instead of `(page - 1) * page_size` (off-by-one), or if the COUNT query uses a different WHERE than the SELECT (e.g., missing the date filter), inflating or deflating `total_count`.

- page_size boundary 1 and 100 are accepted: getDashboard with `page_size` = 1 returns exactly one row; `page_size` = 100 is accepted without error — fails if the validation uses `> 100` correctly but `page_size < 1` accidentally rejects 1, or if the cap is applied as `Math.min(page_size, 99)`.

- page_size of 0 or 101 raises ValidationError with code `validation_error`: getDashboard with `page_size` = 0 and separately `page_size` = 101 each throw an error whose `code` property is `"validation_error"` — fails if the guard is missing (query executes with LIMIT 0 or an unbounded page), or if the thrown error uses a generic `Error` without the `code` field.

- page < 1 raises ValidationError: getDashboard with `page` = 0 throws with code `"validation_error"` — fails if the check is `page < 0` (allowing page 0 which produces a negative offset), or if the error is a 500 `Error` rather than the typed validation error.

- date_from equal to date_to raises InvalidDateRangeError with code `invalid_date_range`: getDashboard with both set to the same timestamp throws the typed error — fails if the comparison is `>` instead of `>=` (allowing an empty-but-not-invalid range to slip through and return zero rows with a 200), or if the error class lacks the `code` field.

- unknown company_id in getDashboard raises ResourceNotFoundError with code `resource_not_found`: getDashboard for a UUID that has no row in `company_financial_totals` throws the typed error with the company_id in `details` — fails if the service skips the existence check and returns an empty page (200 with `data: []`), making a typo indistinguishable from "no results".

- unknown worker_id in simulateWrite raises ResourceNotFoundError: simulateWrite with a `worker_id` that has no matching row throws before any source or projection write occurs — fails if the worker check is inside the transaction after the `paymentOrder.create`, leaving an orphan source row on rollback failure, or if the error is a generic 500.

- getCompanyTotals for an unknown company raises ResourceNotFoundError: calling the service directly with a UUID absent from `company_financial_totals` throws with code `"resource_not_found"` and the id in `details` — fails if the method returns a zero-filled object (total_amount `"0"`, count 0) instead of signalling absence, masking the not-found case.

- projection row is read back from within the transaction (not via the outer client): simulateWrite returns an `OperationRow` whose `status` matches the input and whose `created_at` is non-null — fails if the read-back uses `this.prisma.operation.findUnique` (non-transactional) instead of `tx.operation.findUnique`, so under a concurrent re-derive the returned row could be the old value, or if the repository method `getOperationByOrderId` (which uses the outer client) is called after commit and a concurrent re-derive has already overwritten the row with a stale snapshot.

Not tested in this file: re-derivation idempotency and window repair (`test/re-derivation.spec.ts`), drift-repair detection/skip/recompute (`test/drift-repair.spec.ts`), and the Prisma migration DDL itself — those have their own spec files per the plan's manifest.

import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach } from "vitest";
import { Prisma, Decimal } from "@prisma/client";
import { OperationsService } from "../src/operations/operations.service";
import type {
  OperationRow,
  DashboardQuery,
  DashboardResult,
  CompanyTotals,
  SimulateWriteInput,
  OrderStatus,
} from "../src/operations/operations.types";
import {
  ResourceNotFoundError,
  InvalidDateRangeError,
  ValidationError,
} from "../src/operations/operations.types";

// In-memory state to simulate the database
interface PaymentOrder {
  id: string;
  companyId: string;
  workerId: string;
  status: string;
  amount: Decimal;
  currency: string;
  createdAt: Date;
  updatedAt: Date;
}

interface OperationProjection {
  orderId: string;
  companyId: string;
  status: string;
  amount: Decimal;
  currency: string;
  workerName: string;
  workerRole: string;
  lastEventType: string | null;
  createdAt: Date;
}

interface CompanyTotal {
  companyId: string;
  totalAmount: Decimal;
  orderCount: number;
}

interface Worker {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  role: string;
}

interface OrderEvent {
  orderId: string;
  eventType: string;
  createdAt: Date;
}

class InMemoryDB {
  paymentOrders = new Map<string, PaymentOrder>();
  operations = new Map<string, OperationProjection>();
  companyTotals = new Map<string, CompanyTotal>();
  workers = new Map<string, Worker>();
  events: OrderEvent[] = [];

  // Transaction tracking for concurrency testing
  private pendingTransactions: Array<() => void> = [];

  createMockTx(): any {
    const db = this;
    return {
      paymentOrder: {
        findUnique: async ({ where }: { where: { id: string } }) => {
          const order = db.paymentOrders.get(where.id);
          return order ? { ...order } : null;
        },
        create: async ({ data }: { data: Partial<PaymentOrder> }) => {
          const order: PaymentOrder = {
            id: data.id!,
            companyId: data.companyId!,
            workerId: data.workerId!,
            status: data.status!,
            amount: data.amount! as Decimal,
            currency: data.currency!,
            createdAt: data.createdAt ?? new Date(),
            updatedAt: data.updatedAt ?? new Date(),
          };
          db.paymentOrders.set(order.id, order);
          return { ...order };
        },
        update: async ({ where, data }: { where: { id: string }; data: Partial<PaymentOrder> }) => {
          const existing = db.paymentOrders.get(where.id);
          if (!existing) throw new Error("Order not found");
          const updated = { ...existing, ...data };
          db.paymentOrders.set(where.id, updated);
          return { ...updated };
        },
      },
      operation: {
        findUnique: async ({ where }: { where: { orderId: string } }) => {
          const op = db.operations.get(where.orderId);
          return op ? { ...op } : null;
        },
      },
    };
  }
}
```

```ts
class TestContext {
  // Simulated DB state
  paymentOrders = new Map<string, any>();
  operations = new Map<string, any>();
  companyTotals = new Map<string, { totalAmount: Decimal; orderCount: number }>();
  workers = new Map<string, Worker>();
  events: OrderEvent[] = [];

  // Mock repository
  repo: any;
  
  // Mock prisma client
  prisma: any;

  constructor() {
    this.repo = this.createMockRepo();
    this.prisma = this.createMockPrisma();
  }

  private createMockRepo() {
    const self = this;
    return {
      findWorkerById: async (id: string) => self.workers.get(id) ?? null,
      findLastEventForOrder: async (orderId: string) => {
        const evts = self.events.filter(e => e.orderId === orderId);
        if (evts.length === 0) return null;
        return evts[evts.length - 1].eventType;
      },
      upsertOperation: async (tx: any, input: SimulateWriteInput, worker: Worker, lastEventType: string | null) => {
        self.operations.set(input.order_id, {
          orderId: input.order_id,
          companyId: input.company_id,
          status: input.status,
          amount: new Decimal(input.amount),
          currency: input.currency,
          workerName: worker.name,
          workerRole: worker.role,
          lastEventType,
          createdAt: self.paymentOrders.get(input.order_id)?.createdAt ?? new Date(),
        });
      },
      upsertCompanyTotal: async (tx: any, companyId: string, deltaAmount: string, deltaCount: number) => {
        const existing = self.companyTotals.get(companyId);
        if (!existing) {
          self.companyTotals.set(companyId, {
            totalAmount: new Decimal(deltaAmount),
            orderCount: deltaCount,
          });
        } else {
          existing.totalAmount = existing.totalAmount.plus(new Decimal(deltaAmount));
          existing.orderCount += deltaCount;
        }
      },
      getCompanyTotal: async (companyId: string) => {
        const t = self.companyTotals.get(companyId);
        if (!t) return null;
        return {
          company_id: companyId,
          total_amount: t.totalAmount.toString(),
          order_count: t.orderCount,
        };
      },
      queryDashboard: async (query: DashboardQuery) => {
        let rows = Array.from(self.operations.values()).filter(op => op.companyId === query.company_id);
        
        if (query.status) {
          rows = rows.filter(op => op.status === query.status);
        }
        if (query.date_from) {
          rows = rows.filter(op => op.createdAt >= query.date_from!);
        }
        if (query.date_to) {
          rows = rows.filter(op => op.createdAt <= query.date_to!);
        }
        
        rows.sort((a, b) => b.createdAt.getTime() - a.createdAt.getTime() || (b.orderId > a.orderId ? 1 : -1));
        
        const total_count = rows.length;
        const offset = (query.page - 1) * query.page_size;
        const pageRows = rows.slice(offset, offset + query.page_size);
        
        return {
          data: pageRows.map(op => ({
            order_id: op.orderId,
            company_id: op.companyId,
            status: op.status,
            amount: op.amount.toString(),
            currency: op.currency,
            worker_name: op.workerName,
            worker_role: op.workerRole,
            last_event_type: op.lastEventType,
            created_at: op.createdAt,
          })),
          total_count,
          page: query.page,
          page_size: query.page_size,
        };
      },
    };
  }

  private createMockPrisma() {
    const self = this;
    return {
      $transaction: async (callback: (tx: any) => Promise<any>) => {
        const tx = {
          paymentOrder: {
            findUnique: async ({ where }: any) => {
              const order = self.paymentOrders.get(where.id);
              return order ? { ...order } : null;
            },
            create: async ({ data }: any) => {
              const order = { ...data };
              self.paymentOrders.set(order.id, order);
              return { ...order };
            },
            update: async ({ where, data }: any) => {
              const existing = self.paymentOrders.get(where.id);
              if (!existing) throw new Error("Not found");
              const updated = { ...existing, ...data };
              self.paymentOrders.set(where.id, updated);
              return { ...updated };
            },
          },
          operation: {
            findUnique: async ({ where }: any) => {
              const op = self.operations.get(where.orderId);
              return op ? { ...op } : null;
            },
          },
        };
        return callback(tx);
      },
    };
  }
}
```

```ts
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach } from "vitest";
import { Decimal } from "@prisma/client";
import { OperationsService } from "../src/operations/operations.service";
import type { ... } from "../src/operations/operations.types";
import { ResourceNotFoundError, InvalidDateRangeError, ValidationError } from "../src/operations/operations.types";

// ... in-memory DB and mock setup ...

describe("OperationsService", () => {
  let ctx: TestContext;
  let service: OperationsService;

  beforeEach(() => {
    ctx = new TestContext();
    service = new OperationsService(ctx.repo, ctx.prisma);
  });

  describe("read-your-own-writes", () => {
    it("simulateWrite inserts a new order, getDashboard includes it", async () => {
      // Seed worker
      ctx.workers.set("w1", { id: "w1", name: "Alice", role: "driver" });
      
      // Write
      const result = await service.simulateWrite({
        order_id: "o1",
        company_id: "c1",
        worker_id: "w1",
        status: "pending",
        amount: "100.00",
        currency: "USD",
      });
      
      // Read back via dashboard
      const dashboard = await service.getDashboard({
        company_id: "c1",
        page: 1,
        page_size: 10,
      });
      
      expect(dashboard.data).toHaveLength(1);
      expect(dashboard.data[0].order_id).toBe("o1");
      expect(dashboard.data[0].status).toBe("pending");
      expect(dashboard.data[0].amount).toBe("100.00");
    });

    it("simulateWrite update changes status, getDashboard reflects new status", async () => {
      // Seed worker
      ctx.workers.set("w1", { id: "w1", name: "Alice", role: "driver" });
      
      // First write: insert as pending
      await service.simulateWrite({
        order_id: "o1",
        company_id: "c1",
        worker_id: "w1",
        status: "pending",
        amount: "100.00",
        currency: "USD",
      });
      
      // Second write: update to approved
      await service.simulateWrite({
        order_id: "o1",
        company_id: "c1",
        worker_id: "w1",
        status: "approved",
        amount: "100.00",
        currency: "USD",
      });
      
      // Dashboard shows approved
      const dashboard = await service.getDashboard({
        company_id: "c1",
        page: 1,
        page_size: 10,
      });
      
      expect(dashboard.data).toHaveLength(1);
      expect(dashboard.data[0].status).toBe("approved");
    });
  });

  describe("concurrent totals", () => {
    it("two concurrent inserts for same company produce correct total", async () => {
      ctx.workers.set("w1", { id: "w1", name: "Alice", role: "driver" });
      
      await Promise.all([
        service.simulateWrite({
          order_id: "o1", company_id: "c1", worker_id: "w1",
          status: "pending", amount: "100.00", currency: "USD",
